h1: P.A. Place Hotel Nakhon Sawan — a 3-star hotel in downtown Pak Nam Pho with clean rooms and great value
intro: If you want to stay in central Pak Nam Pho, within walking distance of restaurants and the market, without paying a lot — P.A. Place Hotel is a name travellers passing through Nakhon Sawan mention often for value. It's a 3-star hotel on Suwannawit Road, close to the Chao Phraya River and Sawan Park, with clean rooms, cold air-con and free parking. It's not a shiny new boutique, but with strong review scores and rooms from around ฿600/night, it's a downtown pick many guests come back to.

body.html: What makes P.A. Place Hotel a go-to for travellers is its central location in downtown Pak Nam Pho on Suwannawit Road. It's just a few minutes' drive from the Chao Phraya River and Sawan Park, and an easy walk into the shopping streets and Pak Nam Pho market. For anyone driving from Bangkok up north who wants to stay downtown for a night, or anyone in town on business, this is a spot where you can find food and stroll around easily.

The hotel is a mid-size 3-star building of around 78 rooms. What guests praise most is the rooms being clean, a good size, and the air-con being properly cold. There's an in-house restaurant, a small lounge bar, free parking, a lift, a 24-hour reception desk, and complimentary coffee and cocoa in the morning. It positions itself as a practical downtown stay rather than a luxury one, but it handles the basics well enough to earn high review scores.

Rooms come in several types, from a Standard Twin with two beds, to a Standard Queen, up to a Deluxe Queen. Every room is air-conditioned with a TV, fridge, water heater and work desk, and some have a microwave and kettle. The Standard rooms suit a one-night stay where value matters most, while the Deluxe Queen is roomier if you want to sleep more comfortably. Many reviews note the rooms are odour-free and consistently clean — something hotels at this price don't always manage.
"Clean, spacious room, very cold air-con, central location with food within walking distance, free parking, great value, and helpful staff."

To be honest, the main thing reviewers flag is consistency between rooms. Some guests get a great first room but find a second room that doesn't quite match, or a water heater that isn't working in certain rooms. A few also mention that the hourly late-checkout fee felt more expensive than expected, and that some staff could still improve their communication. These are small things worth knowing, but they don't sink the overall picture.

Another thing to know before you book is that this is an older hotel in town, not a new-design property. If you're expecting a boutique feel or full resort-style facilities, this isn't it. But measured on cleanliness, a central location, free parking and an affordable price, it does the job of a good-value downtown hotel well.

Overall, P.A. Place Hotel scores around 8.6 out of 10 on Trip.com (152 reviews) and similarly high on Agoda from several thousand guests. It won't wow you on design, but if you want a downtown Pak Nam Pho stay with clean rooms, cold air-con, free parking and a price from around ฿600 rising to roughly ฿900 by room type — it's a value downtown pick that guests return to often.

A tip from the reviews: for the best-condition room, ask for the Deluxe Queen and check the water heater and air-con on arrival. If it's not right, ask to switch straight away. Clarify the late-checkout fee in advance if you plan to leave late, and if you're driving, the downtown location has free parking, though you may need to circle a bit when it's busy.

faqTitle: FAQ — P.A. Place Hotel Nakhon Sawan

faq.q: Where is P.A. Place Hotel in Nakhon Sawan, and what's nearby?
faq.a: P.A. Place Hotel is at 276/4 Suwannawit Road, Pak Nam Pho, in central Nakhon Sawan. It's about 5 minutes' drive from the Chao Phraya River source, Sawan Park and Pak Nam Pho market, and an easy walk to the shopping streets — handy both for stopovers and for business in town.

faq.q: How much does P.A. Place Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿600/night for a Standard Twin. Choices run from Standard Twin and Standard Queen up to the roomier Deluxe Queen. Rates rise by room type to roughly ฿850–900 — always compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does P.A. Place Hotel have parking?
faq.a: Yes — free on-site parking, with a 24-hour reception that handles late check-ins. It's a plus for drivers passing through Nakhon Sawan who want a downtown stay with easy parking, though you may need to circle a little when it's busy.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at P.A. Place Hotel — are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are air-conditioned with a TV, fridge, water heater and work desk. What guests praise most is the rooms being clean, odour-free and the air-con properly cold. Condition can be a little inconsistent room to room, so ask for the Deluxe Queen and check the water heater and air-con on arrival.

faq.q: Who is P.A. Place Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for anyone wanting a clean, good-value stay in downtown Pak Nam Pho — both stopover travellers on the Bangkok–Chiang Mai route and people in town on business. It's less suited to those after a new-design property or full resort-style facilities.

faq.q: Does P.A. Place Hotel serve breakfast or other extras?
faq.a: The hotel has an in-house restaurant and lounge bar, plus complimentary coffee and cocoa from morning into the afternoon, with hot water and a microwave available. Room service is reasonably priced per several reviews, and the central location means restaurants are easy to find nearby.
